Bind CAN3 parameter and PartOpacity channels of one linked-model resource to one explicit CMO3 without changing the active session. Parameters use exact parameter GUID and live2dParam_ attribute ID. Typed source parameter IDs are reported as matchesId/differentId, legacy s labels as legacyText, and empty source maps as null/missing after exact matching. Part GUIDs supply canonical Part IDs; raw source identity remains metadata. Underscore channels report exact mapKey with scene/track/curveId in underscorePartBindings or unboundUnderscorePartCurves; duplicate attribute IDs do not merge channels. Does not verify stored link provenance, play animation, or establish Cubism equivalence.

Edit one existing CAN3 parameter, modern PartOpacity, legacy-colon or underscore-map PartOpacity, or Image/Guide visual scalar anchor value with shared revision, undo/redo and native save. Image/Guide curveId is scalex, scaley, rotate, shear, opacity or artPathWidth, as listed in visualCurves; these channels reject partOpacityMapKey. Guide requires its complete supported track ownership and empty-map layout. Image handles and interpolation-type editing remain unsupported; supported Guide scalar channels also accept handle and type edits. Signed anchorFrame identifies the key; controls, key frames and unknown data stay unchanged. Anchor extrema caches are verified and updated; stored evaluation caches are invalidated. Shared scalar storage is rejected; this raw source edit does not claim Cubism playback equivalence. For underscore-map channels, optional partOpacityMapKey selects the exact raw map key and is required when curveId is ambiguous; a supplied selector never falls back.

Read CAN3 scenes, model tracks and existing parameter keys without changing the active session. scene.imageTracks separately lists image-track identity, timing, visualCurves and pointChannels for stored xy/anchor coordinates. scene.soundTracks lists existing Sound track guid, name, resourceGuid, start, internalOffset and duration for deletion; it does not decode audio or expose volume. scene.guideTracks lists the same identity and timing fields plus six supported visualCurves and pointChannels for stored xy/anchor coordinates of existing GuideImage tracks; guide directories are never opened. Unsupported or malformed Image/Guide scalar channels are omitted; budget exhaustion fails the read. imageResources lists linked image GUIDs and names/sourceFile paths only where stored; paths are literal and never opened. Values and frames retain stored units; control positions and flags are not evaluated. scene.loop, scene.tag and a parameter curve's baseValue appear only where the file stores them. Does not load linked models, play animation, edit keys, or establish Cubism compatibility.
Read supplied-profile CMO3/CAN3 authoring container and model definitions without changing the active session; does not evaluate or render a Cubism model.

Compute in-range mathematical weights on primary LINEAR keyform grids without changing the session. Parameter IDs omitted from parameterValues use active runtime values, or model defaults for path queries; sourceGuid optionally selects one owner. Does not clamp, wrap, evaluate morphs or extended caches, transform coordinates, or produce a Cubism pose.

Add morph geometry, raw Glue intensity, and opacity deltas to primary LINEAR forms in their recorded coordinate spaces without changing the session. Requires an exact normal default corner and non-repeating MORPH_TARGET parameters whose range includes neutral zero. Active SNS_CURVE settings consume validated stored intermediate morph keys; extendedMorphExtensions identifies selected extensions. Inactive caches are preserved; curve regeneration and normal extended caches remain unsupported. Unique full-range constraint curves interpolate linearly and use the smallest controller limit; opacity clamps after all deltas. Supports positions, raw Glue intensity, and raw rotation angle/origin; changed draw order/colors/scale/reflection, ambiguous or partial constraint graphs and ambiguous bases are rejected. Uses active runtime values, or model defaults for path queries, unless parameterValues overrides IDs; sourceGuid optionally selects one owner. Deformer transforms are not evaluated; this is not a Cubism pose.

clampToKeys.description: On a keyform axis of a non-repeating parameter, hold the end keyform when a value lies outside the keyed span, take a value closer than 0.001 to a key as that key (Cubism Core 6.0.1 snaps this way), and report the resulting axisValues; morph-target keys and repeating parameters are not snapped; the default rejects samples outside the span and does not snap.

commands.description: Interpolate primary LINEAR keyform geometry and numeric attributes in their recorded coordinate spaces without changing the session. Uses active runtime values, or model defaults for path queries, unless parameterValues overrides IDs; sourceGuid optionally selects one owner. Preserves separate coordinate representations and raw rotation angles and floating draw order. Does not evaluate morphs, extended caches, deformer transforms, runtime sorting or a Cubism pose.

Read CMO3 source geometry, primary and generated forms, multi-axis grids, morph targets, blend-weight constraints, and texture metadata without changing the session. An ArtPath source lists its stroke settings and the control points of each keyform; it is not evaluated or drawn; its name, ID, parent, clipping masks and control points can be edited, and points added and deleted. The model's brushes list the stored ArtPath brush identifiers, drawing settings and textureInput metadata, including the current input's stored canvas transform. live2d_brush_set edits stored drawing settings and transform coefficients; live2d_brush_replace_image replaces an existing shared image with a same-size static PNG. Generated vertex-count and target-availability flags describe incomplete caches. Non-null morph edit base maps are not decoded. Positions retain source coordinate spaces; this is not an evaluated canvas pose.

Edit the explicit opacity scalar of one primary ArtMesh or ArtPath form in the active CMO3 document, with shared revision and undo/redo. Requires the current expectedRevision and exact owner/form/coordinate identity. Values must fit the native finite float field; authored values are preserved without clamping. ArtPath requires one existing private literal float through private inline form inheritance; missing, aliased, shared, shadowed or nonliteral storage is refused. Unsupported derived forms are rejected. Stored editing does not establish ArtPath rendering or vendor acceptance.

Edit one primary ArtMesh or Warp form vertex in its recorded coordinate space in the active CMO3 document, with shared revision and undo/redo. Requires the current expectedRevision and exact owner/form/coordinate identity. Unsupported shared storage or derived caches are rejected; this does not evaluate a canvas pose.

The clip keeps it as audio: [{path, frame, mute?}], top track first, path resolved to an absolute name. Video export (export_video_start) mixes the tracks that are not muted at full volume, each starting where its frame first shows in the video and playing once, unless the request names its own audio file. An image sequence, frames, GIF, APNG, WebP and still-image exports leave them out, and an INP export drops them. Live playback in the editor plays no sound.

Set the eye blinking track of an INX animation in one undo: a key (frame, value from 0 closed to 1 open, linear between keys) and/or the effect (0 to 100, 100 when unset). While the track has keys, playback, seek, sample and export scale every listed eye parameter toward its minimum by 1 + (value - 1) * effect / 100.

Add a parameter bookmark label to an INX animation in one undo, or replace the one at index (from 0). The clip keeps them as bookmarks: [{label, x, y, parameters}]. Deleting a parameter takes it off every label; an INP export drops them.

Add a parameter controller to an INX animation, pinned to the frontmost Part drawn at (x, y) on the integer `frame` (default 0, before eye blinking); with `end` [x, y], a direction controller from (x, y) to `end`. It moves the listed `parameters`, each one that binds its Part (or the Part of `end`) or a node above it, or all of those by default. One undo step. Read back as the clip's `controllers`.

Bake target tracking: on every integer frame from `from` to `to` (default the whole animation), each controller with a target, in list order, follows it, and its parameters are keyed with the solved values blended by its weight with the frame's values so far, in list order. Then the animation's controllers are removed. One undo step. Refused while freeze is on, and for a lane that would not draw the key, as move is. Answers {from, to, keys, unreached}.
Delete one parameter controller, or every one of the animation without `controller`. A controller that followed a deleted one follows nothing. One undo step.

Move a parameter controller to (x, y) on an integer frame: its parameters are solved, inside their ranges, so that a single-point controller reaches the point or a direction controller turns its end toward it, and keyed on the frame in one undo step. A lane that would not then draw the key from the current parameter values (such as a Stepped lane on a later key) is refused. Answers {reached, distance, keys}.

Read only. Where each parameter controller of an INX animation is on an integer frame, before eye blinking: {name, frame, controllers: [{name, kind, start, end?, parameters, target, extend, weight, broken?}]}. `broken` says why a controller cannot be placed.

Change a parameter controller: the `parameters` it moves, the controller it follows as `target` (null for none), `extend` (whether a line of a direction controller reaches past its ends, default true) and `weight` (0 to 100, how much of the followed result a bake keys). Null `parameters` changes nothing. One undo step.
Create an animation in the shared document history.
Delete an animation in one undo.

Delete form edits of an INX animation: those of `node` (in `mode` only, if given), or all without `node`; with `frame`, only their key on that frame. A form edit left without keys goes. One undo step.

Form animation: key the form edit of `node` on an integer `frame` of an INX animation, without parameters, adding the form edit if the node has none in that adjustment `mode`. Mode 1 (default) offsets the node's own vertices before its parents deform it, so the edit follows the parent's angle; mode 2 offsets a drawn Part or Mask in model coordinates after all deformation and glue. A Part, Mask, GridDeformer or PathDeformer has one offset per vertex or grid point. The key holds `offsets`, or zeros with `reset` (Reset Form Edit), or else what the form edit shows on that frame moved by `delta` [dx, dy] at the listed `vertices` (all by default). With `space` "model" the delta is how far the vertices move in the picture shown, as a viewport drag gives it; in mode 1 it is measured on a drawn Part outside composites, on a frame of the clip that shows form `frame`, so seek one first. `frame` is a form frame, which `animation_form_time` maps clip frames to. One undo step. Seek again to see it. Read back as the clip's `forms`.

Read only. The form edits of an INX animation on an integer frame: {name, frame, formFrame, forms: [{node, mode, keys, offsets | broken}]}, where `formFrame` is the frame the timing curve shows and `broken` says why a form edit is not drawn: a missing node, a node without vertices to edit, a vertex count that changed, or mode 2 on a node that is no drawn Part or Mask or sits inside a composite.

Set the form timing curve of an INX animation (time remapping): each key maps a frame of the clip to the form frame its form edits show there, sampled with `interpolation` (Linear by default, or Nearest, Stepped, Cubic, Bezier). Null or no keys clears it. One undo step. Read back as the clip's `formTime`.

Set stepped exposure for an INX clip or parameterGroup in one undo. Keys contain frame and integer value (hold length 1 to 1000000). A key starts a new hold grid; time before the first key is continuous. Null or empty keyframes clears. The nearest ancestor group's override replaces global stepping for its parameters. Global stepping also affects forms and images, while audio keeps continuous clip time.

Mark lanes of an INX animation frozen in a batch, or turn its freeze on at a frame or off, in one undo. mark all, listed or unlisted marks exactly those lanes; none clears every mark and turns freeze off unless frame is given. frame (an integer frame of the animation) turns freeze on there, null turns it off. While freeze is on, each frozen lane holds its value at that frame in playback and every export, and an edit that changes a frozen lane's keys, interpolation or merge mode, or deletes it, is refused; key all and unkey all pass frozen lanes by.

Add a group track to an INX animation in one undo, up to 32, hidden or locked from the start if asked: groups: [{name, x, y, scale, opacity, hidden?, locked?}]. Image and audio tracks join it with their group field and the model with animation_group_set model: true. A member's position is scaled by the group's scale and moved by its x, y; the opacities multiply.
Remove a group track of an INX animation in one undo; its members stay, out of the group. A locked group is refused.

Change a group track of an INX animation in one undo: placement (x, y, scale, opacity), hidden (a hidden group's members, the model included, are not exported), locked (its members cannot be changed either), and model (true puts the model in the group as the clip's modelGroup, false takes it out). A locked group only changes in a request that unlocks it.

Add an image track (a background, or a foreground with front) to an INX animation in one undo: a PNG, TGA or baseline JPEG file, up to 8 tracks a clip. The clip keeps it as images: [{path, x, y, scale, opacity, front?, hidden?, locked?, group?}], top track first, path resolved to an absolute name. x and y place the image's centre in world units (default 0), scale is world units per image pixel (default 1), opacity 0 to 1 (default 1). Video, frames and GIF exports of the clip draw the tracks behind the model (in front with front), the top track over the lower ones; a hidden track is not exported. Still image and INP exports leave them out. The editor draws image tracks while an image sequence is present in the active clip, including guides; Solo and onion-skin views omit these overlays.
Remove an image track of an INX animation in one undo; a locked track, or one in a locked group, is refused. index counts from 0 in the clip's images list.

Read the source image selected by every sequence track at a clip frame without changing the session: images contains index, path (null for a gap), sourceFrame, gap and guide. Global frame stepping is applied before image remapping.

Add a numbered PNG/JPEG image sequence with name, directory and prefix, or reload an existing sequence with name and index. Numeric suffix gaps remain blank exposures. Reload preserves the source-frame origin and timing. Files remain external links; export_collect copies them. One undo; locked tracks and groups refuse reload.

Change an image track of an INX animation in one undo: placement (x, y, scale, opacity), front, hidden, locked, guide (preview only, omitted from exports), its group (a name, or null to leave it) and its place in the list (to, an index). A locked track only changes in a request that unlocks it (locked: false); a track in a locked group does not change until the group is unlocked. index counts from 0 in the clip's images list.

Set a sequence track's timeRemap curve in one undo. Each key maps a clip frame to a zero-based source offset from firstNumber; fractional offsets hold the preceding image, and missing or out-of-range offsets are blank. Without a curve, source time follows the clip. Null or empty keyframes clears the curve. Exact keys take effect on their frame.
Add a keyframe at a frame using the parameter's current value, in one undo.

Key all: add a keyframe at a frame of an INX animation for every listed parameter (every parameter of the model without a list), each axis using the parameter's current value, in one undo. A key already on the frame takes the new value.
Copy one parameter's animation keys at a frame into the session key clipboard.
Delete a parameter-axis key at a frame in one undo.
Unkey all: delete every key on a frame of an INX animation (only the keys of the listed parameters with a list) in one undo. The lanes stay. Refused when no key is on the frame.
Paste the session key clipboard into a parameter at a frame in one undo.
Set a parameter-axis animation key without changing other lanes.
Delete a parameter-axis lane and its keys in one undo.

Set a parameter-axis lane's interpolation, merge mode, shy mark or freeze mark in one undo. A shy lane is hidden from the editor timeline while the animation's shy is on (animation_shy_set); a frozen lane holds its value at the freeze frame while freeze is on (animation_freeze_set).
Delete the marker on a frame of an INX animation in one undo. A locked marker is refused.

Put a marker (a note of at most 256 characters, may be empty) on a frame of an INX animation in one undo, or replace the text of the marker already there. Markers are kept in the clip as markers: [{frame, text}] sorted by frame, one per frame. They travel with the clip, so a saved file and an INP export carry them. A new marker needs text. On an existing marker, to moves it to a free frame and locked: true or false sets its lock, each with or without text, all in the same undo. A locked marker (locked: true in the list) refuses a new text, a move and a delete until a request carries locked: false.

Bake speech lip sync (INX): key the mouth shapes of the finished analysis job `job` on every frame `from` to `to` of the animation `name` (default the whole recording starting where its audio track `audio_index` begins, one frame past the end keyed to the rest shape X) as Linear/Forced keys, in one undo step. `mappings` is a nonempty list of at most 32 entries {parameter (a leaf parameter UUID), axis (0 or 1), shapes {A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, X: value}}: every shape is required and each value must be a finite f32 inside the parameter's axis range. Cues are half-open [start, end) at audio time (frame - audio frame) * timestep. With `extend` true the clip may be lengthened to reach `to`. The WAV the track names must still be the analyzed file with unchanged bytes. A stale or running job, a muted/group-hidden/group-locked track, an additive or weighted clip, a freeze, a lane that is not Linear/Forced, frame stepping or a blink track over a mapped parameter refuses the bake without changing anything. Answers {name, job, audio_index, from, to, frames, keys, parameters, length}.
Ask a running speech analysis to stop; the analyzer is killed and reaped. A finished, failed or already cancelled job is returned unchanged. Answers the same object as animation_motionsync_status.

Start an offline mouth-shape analysis (ANI26) of the local WAV file `path` (RIFF/WAVE, resolved to a canonical name, at most 64 MiB) with the external Rhubarb Lip Sync executable on a worker thread, and return its job id; poll animation_motionsync_status. One analysis runs at a time. `recognizer` is phonetic (default, for non-English audio; documented as less precise) or pocketSphinx (English). The program, its options and its timeout are host settings (SOUL2D_RHUBARB or `rhubarb` on PATH), never request fields. The document, its history and the preview do not change. Answers {job, state: 'running', backend: 'rhubarb', recognizer, path}.

Report a speech-analysis job without blocking: running, finished (with duration and cues [{start, end, value}] of half-open spans in seconds, values one of the Rhubarb shapes A-H/X), failed (with error) or cancelled. Answers {job, state, backend, recognizer, path, ...}; an unknown job is an error.

Onion skin: a PNG of the puppet at a frame over the frames before it (red) and after it (blue), each fainter the further it is. before and after count the ghost frames (default 2 each, at most 8), step is the frames between them (default 1), opacity is the nearest ghost's (default 0.3), size the longest side (16 to 4096, default 1024). bounds, width and height together draw a given view instead (the editor's camera). Optional path also writes the PNG. The session is unchanged. INX documents.

Bake physics (INX): simulate the enabled SimplePhysics drivers of the animation `name` and key their output parameters on every integer frame `from` to `to` (default the whole clip) as Linear/Forced keys, in one undo step. `parameters` limits the bake to those SimplePhysics outputs (default all of them). With `warmup` (default true) the whole clip plays once to settle the physics before the replay that the keys come from, as the Cubism manual's physics bake does. An enabled PathDeformer driver, form edits or form timing, a freeze, an additive or weighted clip, an output lane that is not Linear/Forced, or a simulated value outside the parameter's range refuses the bake without changing anything. Answers {name, from, to, frames, keys, parameters, warmup}.
Delete a physics playlist in one undo. Result {playlists, sceneGroups}.

Preview a physics playlist at time seconds (clamped to its length, the sum of its entries, each as long as its longest clip) without changing the document; animation_advance then plays it on, looping unless loop is false, and physics_step shows the physics. Clip forms are not previewed. The snapshot's playlist field shows {name, time}.

Create or replace a physics playlist (PHY03) in one undo: entries play one after another, each {animation} (an INX clip) or {group} (a scene group); 1 to 256 entries. Stored in the model as playlists. Result {playlists, sceneGroups}.

Start recording live parameter changes into an INX animation (PAR09): from now until animation_record_stop, every value_set is sampled at the clip frame its wall-clock time reaches (frame, default 0, plus elapsed seconds / timestep). Nothing changes in the document until the stop. Refused while a recording runs. Result {name, frame}.
Read the live recording: {recording:false} or {recording:true, name, startFrame, frame (the current one), samples}.

Stop the recording. Unless discard, every recorded parameter is keyed in one undo on all its axes: its value before the recording on the start frame, then the last value set within each later frame; frames past the clip end are dropped. Result {name, parameters, keys, dropped} or, with discard, {name, discarded}.
Rename an animation while preserving its lanes and keys.
Stop animation preview (or a random pose) and restore manual parameter values.
Sample animation values without changing the session.
Delete a scene group in one undo; refused while a playlist holds it. Result {playlists, sceneGroups}.

Create or replace a scene group in one undo: its clips play at once, applied in order; type overwrite (default) moves each parameter the clip animates toward the clip's value by weight/100, add adds the clip's offset from the parameter default times weight/100 (weight 0 to 100, default 100). Stored in the model as sceneGroups. Result {playlists, sceneGroups}.
Preview an animation frame without changing document history.
Edit animation timing, playback properties and loop editing in one undo.

Mark lanes of an INX animation shy in a batch, or turn its shy on or off, in one undo. mark all marks every lane; unkeyed, listed and unlisted mark exactly the lanes without keys, of the listed parameters, or of the others, and turn shy on; none clears every mark and turns shy off. active sets shy on or off and overrides what the mark does. While shy is on, the editor timeline hides shy lanes; they still play, export and take part in Key all and Unkey all.

Insert the keys of a saved animation template into an INX animation from the integer frame on, in one undo. Each template lane goes to the parameter with the same name and axis; a name two parameters share is refused. Answers {applied, lanes, unmatched, dropped}: the keys written, the parameter UUIDs and axes they went to, the template's parameter names and axes no parameter matches, and the keys past the end of the animation, which are left out. A new lane is Linear and Forced. An apply that changes nothing adds no undo step. A frozen lane refuses the whole apply.
Delete a saved animation template. A name that is not saved is refused. There is no undo step.
List the saved animation templates as {presets: {template: {length, lanes: [{parameter, axis, keyframes}]}}}. The resource resource://soul2d/animation/templates returns the same.

Keep the keys of an INX animation from frame `from` to `to` (inclusive) as an animation template named `template`, in animation-templates.json of the settings directory. Every lane with a key in the range is kept, or only the lanes of `parameters`; a lane is kept under its parameter's name, with frames counted from `from`, at most 100000 frames. A saved name is replaced only with overwrite. Answers {template, entry, replaced}. The document is unchanged and there is no undo step.

Vertex trajectories: the world-space positions of vertices of one Part at each frame from from to to (default the whole animation), step frames apart (default 1, or more for a clip over 2000 frames; at most 2000 frames). vertices lists indices (default every vertex, every few-th one for a mesh over 256). Read only. INX documents.

Plan the texture atlases D's INP export would build from the Part textures and meshes, without changing the session. Pages are up to 8192 pixels a side (larger than the 16M-pixel texture limit, so Soul2D itself does not draw such an exported file). Parts with a manual place (atlas_layout_set) keep it and the rest are packed around them. preview (an atlas index) adds preview, that page's albedo as a base64 PNG at most 512 pixels a side.
Return Parts to automatic packing in one undo: parts lists Part UUIDs, or none to clear every manual place. Result {atlasLayout}.

Place Parts by hand in the atlas layout (IO04) in one undo: each {id, atlas, x, y, scale?} puts the Part's pixels (padding excluded) with their top left at x, y on page atlas (0 to 15), at scale texels per texture pixel (default: the packing scale). Stored as model atlasLayout.parts; atlas_build and export_inp keep the places and pack the other Parts around them, and refuse places that overlap or leave the page. Result {atlasLayout}.
Plan best-short-side-fit MaxRects placements for rectangles in a fixed atlas without changing the session.

Generate a Part mesh from its texture alpha with the grid, contour, optimum or skeleton automesher. Option fields are clamped to their documented ranges. preset (contour and optimum only) names a built-in preset (Normal parts, Detailed mesh, Large parts, Small parts, Thin and minimum parts, Preserve edges) or one saved with automesh_preset_save; an option field of the call replaces that field of the preset. Replaces mesh.verts, uvs and indices as one undo step; a Part with deform bindings, welds or depth data is rejected. When the algorithm finds nothing to mesh (skeleton on a shape that thins to a point, contour with too few vertices) the call is not an error: it answers {changed:false, message:"no mesh generated"} and the Part keeps its mesh. Check changed and try another algorithm.
Delete a preset that automesh_preset_save kept. A name that is not saved is refused, and so is a built-in name.

List the presets automesh_preset_save kept, as {presets: {name: {algorithm, preset?, option fields}}}. The built-in presets are not listed. The resource resource://soul2d/automesh/presets returns the same. The three preset tools answer with any document open.

Keep the option fields of a contour or optimum automesh call under name, for automesh_generate and the automesh of split_apply to use as preset. preset may name the built-in preset the fields start from. The presets belong to the user of this machine, not to the document: they are a file in the settings directory, and the call changes no document and adds no undo step. A saved name is replaced only with overwrite:true, and the answer then holds replaced:true. Refused: a built-in name, a name that is not 1 to 64 characters, has a control character anywhere or white space at either end, presets that would make the file larger than 1 MiB, the algorithms grid and skeleton, a field that automesh_generate refuses, a 65th preset, and a host without a settings directory.
Copy the keypoint of bindings (all of the parameter's when bindings is omitted) into the session clipboard.
Copy the keypoint of bindings on one node to a compatible node in one undo.

Edit one keypoint of bindings: unset, reset, set_current, invert, mirror_horizontal, mirror_vertical, flip_deform, symmetrize_deform or set_from_mirror_horizontal / _vertical / _diagonal / _1d (these use the document's flip pairs; _1d pulls from the partner without bindings and pushes to it with them).

Multiple Keys Editing: every set key of every binding of nodes on channel (opacity, zSort, tint or screenTint) in parameters (default all) becomes value (method overwrite, the default), itself plus value (add) or, for tint and screenTint, itself multiplied or screened by value. value is one number, or [r,g,b] for a colour. Opacity and colours are clamped to 0..1. Result {changed}: the number of keys changed. One undo step; nothing changes when no key matches.

commands.description: Paste the copied binding keypoint into the parameter at key in one undo; bindings select the targets (Paste Form Special: only those channels). ratio in [0,1] blends instead (Blend Form): current + ratio × (copied − current). invert {axis: vertical|horizontal, origin?} mirrors a pasted deform shape about that line in node space (default origin: centre of the node's rest bounds), negates a pasted transform.r.z and reflects a pasted transform.t.x (vertical) or t.y (horizontal) position about origin in the parent's space (default 0). Copy a key and paste it back with invert to Reflect it.
Remove bindings (node + param_name) from a parameter in one undo.
Set vertex offsets at a parameter key for undriven nodes.
Set the interpolation mode (Nearest, Linear, Cubic) of bindings in one undo.
Set node transform bindings at a 2D parameter key.

rotation_x.description: Pitch binding in radians, added to transform.r.x.

rotation_y.description: Yaw binding in radians, added to transform.r.y.

commands.description: Swap the keypoint of bindings on one node with those of a compatible node in one undo.

Blend-shape weight limits: the deform binding of node on parameter is scaled by the smallest weight its limits give. Each limit is {parameter, points: [[value, weight], ...]}, 2 to 5 points with rising values and weights in 0..1 over another parameter's first axis, linear between points and flat outside them. An empty limits list removes them. One undo step.
Frame the evaluated world geometry with a small margin.
Run a read-only binary-mask query (distance transform, thinning, longest path, contours) without changing the session.

Lock or unlock the default forms (Cubism "Lock default forms") of an INX document. While locked, an edit that changes or unsets a keyform set at a parameter's default value is refused. Not saved and not an undo step; a new document starts unlocked. Read back as defaultFormLocked.
Write the next whole cells of a pending all-keypoints deform refresh.

Deform-mode tool gesture on the keypoint key of a parameter, written as one undo step through binding_set_deform. tool is translate {delta}, reset, brush {brush, stroke, flow?, snapAxis?}, inflate {brush, samples:[{center,amount}]}, path_deform {path, target, resolution?}, warp {grid: {columns, rows, points}}, perspective {corners}, bezier_translate {index, delta} or bezier_rotate {locked, index, from, to}. warp and perspective are the temporary deform tool (GEO21): warp lays a lattice of (columns+1)x(rows+1) points (1 to 64 cells a side), row-major from the top left, over the bounding box of the vertices and moves them with it, each cell bilinear (one cell zooms, rotates, transforms freely or distorts); perspective moves the box corners (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right) to corners, which must make a convex quad, through a projective map. Inflate applies p += (p-center)*amount*brushWeight to current positions in sample order; finite amount in [-1,1], positive expands and negative contracts. At most 4096 samples. Brush kinds include line {radius, angle}: a strip with positive half-width radius, angle in radians, zero horizontal in node-local coordinates, linear falloff across the strip. The vertices a tool works on come from selected, rect or lasso (brush, inflate, path_deform, warp, perspective and reset default to every vertex; reset with none of them returns the whole key to the rest shape). Optional mirror {horizontal, vertical, origin} and zoom; brush, inflate, path_deform, warp and perspective do not apply mirror. space canvas (translate with selected only, PAR18) reads delta as a canvas move of the vertices as drawn at the current parameter values and solves each vertex's local move through the deformers above it (Newton steps); it answers {id, residual} and is refused, changing nothing, when a vertex does not follow the key at the current values or the solve does not converge. Set the parameter onto the edited key first: between keys the key moves by more than delta. Physics bending a PathDeformer and preview poses are not part of the solve.

Apply one GridDeformer to its children and delete it: its keyed deform offsets are added to each direct child's deform binding on the same parameter, key by key, and the children take its place in the tree with their world transforms kept, so every pose looks the same. Refused for a dynamic or rig-driven grid, a grid with a binding other than deform, a child that is not a Part, Mask, MeshGroup, GridDeformer or PathDeformer, a child that passes the grid on to its own children, a child with a transform binding, and a child that interpolates a shared parameter differently. One undo step.

commands.description: Read a GridDeformer's Bezier control lattice: (3·columns+1) × (3·rows+1) row-major [x, y] points in grid space for divisions [columns, rows] of cubic patches, sampled from the grid at parameter's key (the rest grid without parameter). Edit them and write with deformer_bezier_warp. Read only.

commands.description: Warp a GridDeformer through Bezier handles: each grid point moves to the surface of the controls lattice (as deformer_bezier_controls returns it) at its normalised axis position, and the offsets are written to parameter's key. Handles are not stored; read them again from the key. Divisions that divide the grid evenly reproduce an unedited lattice exactly. One undo step.

commands.description: Create a rotation deformer (INX): a Node marked rotationDeformer {handleLength} at pivot [x, y] in root space with angle radians (transform.r.z, default 0), under parent (default the root), and move children into it keeping their world transforms. Children turn about the pivot when its angle changes or is keyed (transform.r.z bindings). For continuous creation call it once per deformer, passing the previous one as parent. Result {node, children}. One undo step.
Set GridDeformer axes.

commands.description: Extend each GridDeformer in nodes so that no child leaves it: add a grid line outside each side that deformer_validate reports a child past, at the farthest such point. Each added line takes the keyed offsets of the old edge it continues, so the old area and the children outside it move as before. A grid no child leaves is unchanged. One undo step.

commands.description: Generate a face turn (Cubism's automatic face movement, PAR16) on each GridDeformer in nodes: the 1D parameter (for example ParamAngleX for axis x, ParamAngleY for axis y) gets three keys, the middle one the rest grid, the high one turning right (x) or up (y), the low one the other way. Inferred rule, not compared with Cubism: the grid outline stays and a point at normalised position (along, across) in -1..1 moves amount·half·(1-along²)·√(1-across²) along the axis, where half is half the grid's width or height and amount (default 0.3, below 0.5) is the centre's shift. flip reverses the turn. Apply it to the face grid; nested grids follow. A parameter without exactly three keys, the middle one at its default, is refused unless replaceKeys, which sets them to min, default and max. Result {parameter, axis, nodes:[{node, amount}]}. One undo step.

nodes.description: id (one integer UUID), then ids (an array of them), is read in place of nodes when given

commands.description: Generate the humanoid GridDeformer tree (Cubism's automatic deformer generation, GEO13, without part recognition): roles maps role names to mesh UUIDs placed directly in that role. Roles and nesting: Body > Arm L, Arm R, Neck, Head; Head > Face, Front Hair, Side Hair L, Side Hair R, Back Hair; Face > Eye L, Eye R, Brow L, Brow R, Mouth, Nose (inferred, not compared). Each role becomes GridDeformer 'Warp <role>' under parent (default the root) or its parent role, holding its meshes with their world transforms kept, sized to the rest bounds of every mesh under it plus margin (fraction of the larger extent, default 0.05, at least 1 unit) with divisions cells per axis (default 4). A role with no mesh under it is not created and is listed in notGenerated. Result {created:[{role, node}], notGenerated}. Running it again is refused while the 'Warp <role>' names exist. One undo step.

Generate a sway (Cubism's automatic sway, PAR17) on each GridDeformer in nodes: the 1D parameter gets three keys, the middle one the rest grid, the low and high ones swinging the grid away from the fulcrum edge (top, bottom, left or right; default top). Inferred rule, not compared with Cubism: a point at normalised distance d from the fulcrum has weight d^(1+softness) (softness default 1) and moves -horizontal·w / +horizontal·w across the axis (default 15 % of the grid's length along it), vertical·w toward the fulcrum (default 0; negative droops), and zoom·w times its distance from the centre line (default 0). flip swaps the swing. A parameter without exactly three keys, the middle one at its default, is refused unless replaceKeys, which sets them to min, default and max. Result {parameter, nodes:[{node, horizontal}]}. One undo step.

Read only.

Fit a layer's zScale/zOffset so its range on the target lies in a gap: gap adjacent, target, layers (backLayer, frontLayer) or values (back, front); margin; apply=false only reports.
Update a DepthDraw layer: xyOffset/xyScale, backDepth/frontDepth/invert/zScale/zOffset, channel/convolution/customRadius/alphaThreshold, visible/enabled. Fields not given keep their value.

Load a PNG file as a DepthDraw layer (its RGBA is the depth). A saved layer with the same id and size gets the pixels and keeps its settings, its sourcePath too. A relative path names a file beside the open document when one is there, else in the working directory.
